name: com.dveracity/semantic-mcp
title: dVeracity Semantic API
description: Validate emissions data against Open Footprint, check EU CBAM records, query verified methane data

tools.name: semantic_query
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks a specific question about verified oil-and-gas emissions data, e.g. methane for a site or period (PPDM, OGMP 2.0). Call semantic_templates first. Not for general climate questions.

On payment_required, tell your operator what the call needs; do not retry the same call.

tools.name: semantic_templates
tools.description: Use this when you want to see what the verified emissions data can answer, before semantic_query.

tools.name: credits_balance
tools.description: Deprecated: use billing_status (also shows plan and free allowance). Removal planned for 0.9.x.

tools.name: list_standards
tools.description: Use this when you need the standards and versions validate_data can check.

tools.name: validate_data
tools.description:
Use this when a payload needs checking against a non-Open-Footprint standard; call list_standards first. For Open Footprint use ofp_validate.

Only masterData or referenceData.

tools.name: keri_identity
tools.description: Use this when an organisation needs to confirm which verified legal entity and agent identity calls are attributed to. Only with vLEI configured.

tools.name: ofp_models
tools.description:
Use this when building on Open Footprint and you need to know what the model covers. Start here before other ofp_ tools.

The response summary carries the served counts.

tools.name: ofp_search_entities
tools.description:
Use this when you need the Open Footprint entity for a concept ("Scope 3 emissions"). Not for emission factors or calculations.

Matches names, descriptions and fields; ofp_entity gives the full definition.

tools.name: ofp_entity
tools.description:
Use this when you need one entity's fields, types, keys and relationships.

Pass domain when known: ambiguous names fail rather than resolve (ofp_models: ambiguousNameCount).

tools.name: ofp_sectors
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which industries Open Footprint covers or a sector's implementation status.

implemented means a reference implementation exists; planned/placeholder: nothing published.

tools.name: ofp_sector
tools.description: Use this when you need one sector's classification, status and reference artifacts.

tools.name: ofp_policies
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which validation rules apply to a sector's records. For regulations use compliance_policies.

inputs lists e-ledger fields policies read (e.g. co2e_kg), not canonical names. published:false means no rules; never invent guardrails.

tools.name: compliance_policies
tools.description:
Use this when data needs checking against a regulation (e.g. EU CBAM): find the approved policy. For sector rules use ofp_policies.

Only APPROVED policies appear. Empty means none published, not no obligations; never invent rules. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_policy
tools.description:
Use this when you need one approved regulatory policy's rules, provenance and coverage.

Rego only when the source was retained; else rego_unavailable: source_not_retained, the engine cannot load it, and enforcement says whether structured rules run. Never reconstruct Rego. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_evaluate
tools.description:
Use this when an import record or annual EU CBAM declaration (Reg. (EU) 2023/956) needs an approved-policy check before filing. Not for footprint calculations or unlisted regulations.

Runs regulation-derived Rego, not the generic OFP validator. Decision: passed, denied, unevaluable, not_applicable or error (a refusal, never compliance; error.code: policy_not_release_eligible, policy_no_rendered_checks, policy_no_faithful_checks, policy_coverage_inconsistent). A pass covers only the encoded checks: read coverage.note. Requires the compliance:evaluate scope; calls count against the plan limit. CBAM: entity_type cbam_declaration (default carbon_measure), declaration + lines.

tools.name: compliance_evaluation
tools.description:
Use this when a user wants to retrieve or audit a previous evaluation by its id.

Readable only by the caller who ran it. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: compliance_policy_register
tools.description:
Use this when a user asks which provisions of a regulation an evaluation checks.

Encoded vs excluded provisions: a pass says nothing about excluded ones. Requires compliance:read.

tools.name: ofp_validate
tools.description:
Use this when an emissions or footprint record (JSON) needs checking against Open Footprint or sector guardrails before storing or reporting. Not for data-quality questions without a payload.

Checks structure, constraints, enums and calculations; with a sector, its guardrails. Per call read `checked`, `checks_not_run` and `schema.coverage.constraintsDeclared`. Not checked: undeclared ranges, unit coherence, referential integrity, factor provenance. Compliant only if sector_policy is in `checked` and policy.outcome is passed. `schemaValid` is structural; `valid` is deprecated.

tools.name: ofp_semantics
tools.description:
Use this when mapping fields from SAP, an ERP or a supplier feed onto Open Footprint.

High fieldCount is generic; pass maxFieldCount (start at 10) to see only precise codes.

tools.name: ofp_semantic_code
tools.description:
Use this when you have a source-system field and need its place in the Open Footprint model.

Codes on many fields are generic; aligning to one asserts less than it appears.

tools.name: ofp_model_provenance
tools.description: Use this when a user asks which Open Footprint version or extension packs this snapshot serves. Reports the source commit and per-pack id, kind, version, status, core range and regulations. Gate adoption on status: drafts are for review, not adoption.

tools.name: ofp_units
tools.description:
Use this when you need unit codes before converting or validating. No args lists quantity types; quantity lists its units; code resolves one symbol or alias.

detail=full is large; prefer summary. Unresolved codes answer 422 with candidates; unambiguous case/notation variants resolve.

tools.name: ofp_convert
tools.description:
Use this when a measurement needs converting between units (kWh to MJ, bbl to m3). Resolve unsure codes with ofp_units first.

Answers {value, unit, provenance}; keep provenance. A 422 refusal is data: error (unresolved_unit, incompatible_dimension, assumption_required, invalid_conversion_parameters) + detail; read it, do not blind-retry. Volume to energy/mass needs a declared assumption (calorificValue or density); the detail names required fields — never invent. dictionary ([name@]version) is a pin; mismatches refuse. Not CO2e.

tools.name: billing_plans
tools.description:
Use this when you need to know what each dVeracity plan includes or what the free allowance covers.

Show dVeracity plans, what each plan includes and the free-tier allowance.

tools.name: billing_status
tools.description:
Use this when a call was refused for credits or plan, to tell the user what is missing.

Use it after a 402 to tell your human what is missing.
